summary: Refine's documentation build can fail on a fresh install because documentation/package.json imports buffer and lucide-react directly without declaring them; add both before retrying the client build.
symptom: pnpm build fails with Module not found errors for 'buffer' in live-preview and 'lucide-react' in refine-theme.
root_cause: The documentation package uses those modules directly but omits them from its own dependency manifest.
fix: Run pnpm install again before retrying pnpm build.
precheck: Scan documentation/src imports for direct modules not declared in documentation/package.json when the first build fails on fresh install.
anti_pattern: Do not chase webpack config or Node polyfill changes first when the missing-module errors are plain undeclared package dependencies.
quick_checks: If build output shows Can't resolve 'buffer' or 'lucide-react', inspect documentation/package.json before changing the build system.

summary: Garage's official dxflrs/garage image is intentionally shell-less for runtime use, so portable-bundle wrapper images that assume /bin/sh or shell-based entrypoint mutation can fail during build or restart loops even though the original official image path works.
symptom: Bundle packaging attempts that add shell-based wrapper logic fail with Docker build errors or immediate container restart loops before verification can run.
root_cause: The upstream runtime image does not include a shell, so wrapper Dockerfiles and shell entrypoints assume tooling that is absent in the verified official image path.
successful_path: Keep the final portable bundle on the same verified official image path as the primary deployment and package config plus runtime data around it instead of introducing a shell-dependent wrapper image.
fix: Avoid RUN or shell-based entrypoint logic on top of the official image unless you first add the required tooling explicitly.
Prefer reusing the official image directly in the final bundle when the primary deployment already validated that path.
Avoid  or shell-based entrypoint logic on top of the official image unless you first add the required tooling explicitly.
precheck: Inspect the upstream image capabilities before designing a wrapper-image bundle path.
If a bundle image assumes /bin/sh, confirm the base image actually contains it.
If a bundle image assumes , confirm the base image actually contains it.
anti_pattern: Do not replace a validated official-image runtime with an unverified shell wrapper just to satisfy bundle structure preferences.
quick_checks: If Docker build fails on shell commands or the container restart-loops immediately, revert to the official image path and re-verify from bundle artifacts only.
Keep earlier failed packaging attempts in errors.log, but gate success on the final verified path in deploy.log and summary.md.

summary: On hosts that expose only the legacy Docker builder, Helmfile's upstream Dockerfile fails immediately at FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM; use BuildKit/buildx or a compatibility wrapper that removes the automatic platform arg assumption.
symptom: docker build fails before the builder stage starts with an invalid empty platform error on the upstream Dockerfile.
root_cause: The upstream multi-platform Dockerfile relies on BuildKit-provided automatic BUILDPLATFORM values that are absent under the legacy builder.
successful_path: Either use a builder that supports automatic platform args, or provide a host-local compatibility Dockerfile that removes FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM while preserving the upstream build logic.
fix: Detect builder capability before relying on automatic platform args.
When buildx is unavailable, swap to a compatibility Dockerfile rather than repeatedly retrying the same upstream file.
precheck: Run  or otherwise confirm BuildKit/buildx support before using multi-platform Dockerfiles that depend on automatic platform args.
If the host prints the legacy builder deprecation warning, treat  assumptions as suspect.
Run docker buildx version or otherwise confirm BuildKit/buildx support before using multi-platform Dockerfiles that depend on automatic platform args.
If the host prints the legacy builder deprecation warning, treat BUILDPLATFORM assumptions as suspect.
anti_pattern: Do not keep retrying the same upstream Dockerfile with the legacy builder after  fails.
Do not treat the empty-platform parse failure as a source-code compile issue.
Do not keep retrying the same upstream Dockerfile with the legacy builder after the first BUILDPLATFORM parse failure.
quick_checks: If  fails at the first , switch builder strategy immediately.
Record whether buildx is present before deciding to patch or wrap the Dockerfile.
If docker build fails at the first FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM, switch builder strategy immediately.

summary: When packaging Lightdash around the upstream local compose shape, a wrapper service that rebuilds `docker/Dockerfile.headless-browser` wastes time because the Dockerfile is only a `FROM ghcr.io/browserless/chromium:v2.38.2`; use the upstream image directly in the deployment wrapper unless you are intentionally modifying it.
symptom: `docker compose up --build` spends several extra minutes exporting and unpacking a locally tagged headless-browser image even though no custom build steps exist.
root_cause: The upstream helper Dockerfile is a one-line base-image wrapper, so rebuilding it adds export and unpack overhead without changing runtime behavior.
successful_path: Point the wrapper compose service directly at `ghcr.io/browserless/chromium:v2.38.2` and keep the rest of the Lightdash service topology unchanged.
fix: Use the upstream browserless image directly in the wrapper compose file.
Reserve local image builds for cases where the helper Dockerfile adds real filesystem changes or configuration.
precheck: Inspect helper Dockerfiles before enabling `docker compose up --build` in wrappers.
If a Dockerfile is only `FROM <published-image>`, prefer `image:` over `build:` for the wrapper deployment.
anti_pattern: Do not trigger a local build for a no-op helper image during primary deployment.
Do not mistake image-export progress for meaningful application initialization progress when the build has no custom layers.
quick_checks: Open the helper Dockerfile and verify whether it contains anything beyond a single `FROM` line.
If it is a no-op wrapper, switch the compose service to `image:` before the first long build retry.

summary: When two Docker Compose services build from the same Dockerfile target in parallel and export to the same image tag, the build can fail at export time with an image already exists collision.
symptom: Compose builds complete the compile work but fail near export with 'image already exists' when two near-identical services share one output tag.
root_cause: Compose exports each service image independently; parallel services that share the same image tag can collide even if their build inputs are identical.
successful_path: Assign distinct image tags to separately declared sibling services, or build the shared image once and have sibling services reuse it.
fix: Give parallel-built services distinct image tags or build the shared image only once and let sibling services reuse it.
precheck: Inspect compose services that share both build target and image name before the first full build.
anti_pattern: Do not assign the same image tag to multiple services that Compose may export in parallel.
quick_checks: docker compose config | rg '^\s*image:' should show distinct tags for separately declared sibling services built in parallel.
evidence: The MooseFS run initially failed with 'image docker.io/moosefs-local/chunkserver:v4.58.4 already exists' before distinct chunkserver tags fixed the build.

summary: SPIRE's official make build can fail during tidy on a transient google.golang.org/api module zip EOF even when the source and Makefile are correct; retry the official build once before changing targets or patching source.
symptom: make build exits from the tidy stage with EOF fetching google.golang.org/api from the Go proxy.
root_cause: The failure is a transient external module download problem, not a SPIRE source or configuration problem.
successful_path: Rerun the same official make build after the first EOF so the already-cached dependencies are reused; the retry can proceed directly into binary compilation and succeed without source changes.
fix: Retry the official  once after an isolated Go proxy EOF.
Only narrow build targets or patch the build path if repeated retries fail on the same dependency.

precheck: Check whether the failure is an EOF or transport error against a remote Go module before treating it as a SPIRE build regression.
anti_pattern: Do not patch SPIRE source or abandon the official build path after a single transient Go module download EOF.
quick_checks: If the first  fails in , retry once before changing build logic.

summary: For this Hugo static-site target, a Dockerized rebuild with the official Hugo image added slow image pulls and produced cache-key short-read failures, while serving the already validated local public tree through nginx was simpler and reliable.
symptom: Docker build attempts using the official Hugo image spent minutes pulling large layers and then failed with 'failed to compute cache key: short read ... unexpected EOF'.
root_cause: The static artifact had already been validated locally, so rebuilding inside Docker introduced unnecessary large image transfers and a fragile build-context path.
successful_path: Rebuild the site locally with Hugo, keep relative URLs enabled, and package nginx to copy the generated public tree directly instead of rebuilding the site inside Docker.
fix: Switch the serving image to nginx-only and copy the generated public tree.
Add a .dockerignore to exclude git metadata and downloaded artifacts from the build context.
precheck: If the application is a pure static-site artifact and the local build is already validated, ask whether Docker really needs to rebuild the site.
Inspect the Docker build context for large tarballs and .git trees before retrying short-read failures.
anti_pattern: Do not keep retrying a heavyweight builder image path when the validated output is already static and ready to serve.
quick_checks: If Docker build logs fail at cache-key computation after long pulls, inspect whether a prebuilt static output can be copied directly.
Confirm .dockerignore excludes git metadata and downloaded release archives.

summary: Jenkins Remoting source archives can fail Dockerized Maven builds if .git metadata is omitted or Git safe.directory is not configured.
symptom: buildnumber-maven-plugin failed first with 'not a git repository' and then with Git 'dubious ownership' in /build/source-initialized.
root_cause: The Maven lifecycle reads SCM revision data during package, and Docker archive extraction can produce ownership that Git refuses unless safe.directory is configured.
successful_path: For runtime portable delivery, use the official Remoting release artifact; if source building is required, include .git metadata and configure git safe.directory before Maven runs.
fix: Include .git metadata in source snapshots for source builds.
Run git config --global --add safe.directory /build/source-initialized before Maven in Docker.
Prefer the official pinned artifact for Jenkins Remoting runtime bundles.
precheck: Check whether the source snapshot contains .git metadata before attempting Maven package in Docker.
anti_pattern: Do not strip .git from Jenkins Remoting source snapshots if relying on the upstream Maven package lifecycle.
quick_checks: final audit passed after switching to official artifact path
